post.description:
The agent's sign-in password, or without one in the body a password HS makes and shows only here. HS keeps

delete.description: Every token of the agent stops working, its open streams close, and it goes Offline.

post.description:
Agent and stream tokens, and a Plivo browser SDK token Plivo mints for the agent's endpoint, which cannot
outlive them. While the session lives, the agent's calls ring where the browser SDK logs in with it. Its agent
token renews it (POST /me/sessions).
A new endpoint password, set at Plivo and shown once: HS keeps no SIP password. Only for an endpoint HS made.

Ring the agent's SDK login or registered endpoint; the lead is dialed once the agent answers. An agent token
dials only for itself, and only with agent_direct_dial on. Plivo's refusal is the answer (422, or 429 with
Retry-After).

A rating of a call's quality, kept on it under the call's newest primary agent, whoever posts it, and passed to
Plivo's call quality reports, which a Plivo refusal does not undo. A call no agent took has no agent to rate.

The agent leaves the call, as when its phone hangs up; a tenant key leaves as the primary. An agent with a
stint of its own that is not the primary's ends only its own leg. The primary's connected warm consult takes
the caller. Otherwise the call is torn down: the primary's leg ends first, so an outage there leaves the call as
it was, then every other leg, and call.ended reads ended_by agent. A retry, or HS on its own, finishes a teardown
an outage or a refusal cut short, whoever is on the call by then, and sends again each leg Plivo has not confirmed
gone. A call that is over, or that the teardown handed back, is 409 until a queue takes it again.

Put the caller on hold or take it off, or the participant or the transfer's target the body names, or with
`all` every one of them. Each event names the participant or transfer it holds.
Every member comes off hold: the caller, the participants and a transfer's target all talk together.

delete.description:
The supervisor leaves the call, or stops its ring. One on the call leaves once Plivo has hung its leg up, so a
refusal keeps it on the call. A retry hangs its leg up again.

patch.description:
Switch between listen, whisper and barge. The supervisor's mode changes once Plivo has switched it, and a
barge is announced to everyone.

post.description:
A supervisor joins the call to listen, whisper to the agent or barge in. Answers 409 `supervisor_busy` if the
supervisor is on another call, or `omnichannel_not_supported` if the call also texts its caller. A supervisor only
listening or whispering on another call moves here on the same leg. The answer is Plivo's verdict on the ring.

delete.description: The supervisor turns the agent's request for help down.

post.description: The call's agent asks the supervisor on the call for help.
The supervisor mutes or unmutes its own leg, and its mode stays.
A silent listener lets the agent know it is on the call; from then on its events read visible.

Another agent or a phone joins the call, at most two at once; the agent stays the primary and alone may add
or remove one. It rings for 45 seconds, a phone from the business number. Once Plivo takes the ring everyone else
on the call goes on hold, so the agent talks with the participant alone until a merge or a switch.
call.participant_added comes when it joins, with its alias. A call its agent took by transfer, from an agent or
through a queue, takes none.

delete.description:
The participant leaves the call; an agent goes to wrap-up, and one still ringing has its offer cancelled. Either
is told removed. One already off the call has its leg hung up, 422 when Plivo has no such call.

post.description:
Pause or resume the call's recording and each member's own track, answered once each has; resuming what
records nothing starts it. A failure is the answer and emits nothing; a retry finishes what it left.

The agent talks with one member alone, the caller unless the body names a participant or a transfer's target:
every other member goes on hold.

Hand the call over; only its agent or a tenant key may. An agent, up to the tenant's simultaneous agent limit of a
team's free members, or a number is rung into the room: a cold target takes the call when it joins, a warm one
talks with the agent until the transfer completes. A number rings from the business number, and digits after a
`#` are sent once it answers. The request answers once Plivo has taken the ring. A queue, voicemail, a menu or
the tenant's app takes the caller out of the room now, and any supervisor on the call leaves. One transfer at a
time, in a mode the tenant allows; a cold one to a number always is, a warm one only when both are. An agent
token needs agent_direct_dial for a number or a redirect: the tenant's app can dial any number. A saved
destination is the number or redirect it holds, under the same rules.

Stop a transfer that has not completed: its rings are withdrawn and a consult is hung up, and a joined agent
target is told call.participant_removed; the agent keeps the call. Only the agent the transfer came from, or a
tenant key, may stop it. A caller whose agent left while it rang is queued already, and its queue's next round
runs. A transfer has completed once its agent target is the primary, or a target is on the call that its agent
has left, and is completing (409) while Plivo has yet to confirm a complete's hangup of that agent's leg. A retry
waits on a cancelled leg's hangup Plivo has not confirmed; with nothing left to stop, it is 422.

A warm transfer's target takes the call, and the agent leaves to wrap-up; only the agent the transfer came
from, or a tenant key, may complete it. A target on the call takes it once Plivo has hung the agent's leg up, so
a refusal is the answer and the call stays as it was. A target whose join HS has not heard yet is looked for in
Plivo's room: one there is on the call, one still ringing is refused. A repeat changes nothing.

get.description:
Newest first. An agent sees what it handled, a supervisor also what its teams handled and what no agent took
on a route to its teams. `number` takes several, comma-separated: with `limit=1` it reads the newest conversation
with any of them, and its `our_address`. `participant_agent_id` keeps those that agent is on now, in wrap-up too.
`sort=last_activity_at`, `active_after` and `active_before` read a customer's history by its last activity, so they
need `number`.

An agent's SMS, WhatsApp or email to a customer, under POST /calls' rules: an agent token starts one only for

How many of a customer's conversations match the list's filters (`number` is required), and how many of

parameters.name: attribute

post.description:
The closed conversations `/conversations/search` finds for this body, one CSV row each in its order, at most
10,000. `columns` names the search document's fields to write in that order, `conversation_number` last unless
named, and defaults to every field; `created_at` is ISO 8601 in `time_zone`. Needs the role's `download_list`.

Each item of the closed conversations `/conversations/search` finds for this body, in its order and then in
time order: messages, notes, voicemails, recordings, call feedback, task activity, each stint an agent took,
transfers, dispositions and wrap-up notes. A row by an agent the caller does not see is left out, except a
transfer or a note. Times are in `time_zone`. Needs the role's `download_conversation`.

Closed conversations matching every filter given, with the visibility of GET /conversations, newest first unless
`sort` and `order` say otherwise. One word of `text` matches inside any word of the messages, notes, email subjects,
wrap-up notes, disposition names, the state, the customer's address, our number, who ended the call and the names of
the handling agents, their skills and their teams, in any case; several words match
as a phrase whose last word may be cut short. `team_id` finds those teams too. A range takes `gt`, `gte`, `lt`
and `lte`, in seconds, messages or holds. `filter` holds groups of atoms, each joined to the one before it by its entry in
`conditions` (`and` unless given); dates and times of day are read in `time_zone`. Each hit carries the values of
the filter fields `fields` names in its own `fields`.

patch.description:
`attributes` merge one level deep: a key replaces the stored one, null removes it. At most 2 KB, in any state.
`waiting` marks a live text conversation the caller is on (409 not_text, not_live), until the next message;
false unmarks it, and a `waiting` that reads as it is now is a no-op. A new `customer` corrects who the customer is:
replies and the customer's next messages follow it (422 invalid_customer for one that is no address of the
channel; 409 when that customer already has another open conversation on this line).

post.description:
End a text conversation: its offers are withdrawn as cancelled, its agents go to wrap-up, and it closes as
agent_closed after their wrap-up, or as cancelled when no agent ever took it. A second agent or a warm transfer's
joined target is told it was removed.

The customer's satisfaction answer, as text, from a survey after the agent, in any state: the latest answer
stands, and a survey that got none (no `score`) reads `No Response` until one comes.

get.description: Oldest first. An agent's read of the last page clears the conversation's unread count.

post.description:
An agent's message while its own assignment is active, or files alone in its wrap-up (409 in_wrap_up for text),
or a tenant key's as the primary agent's (409 not_live without one). `channel`, `to` and `from` move it to another
line: SMS, WhatsApp or email to the customer, or to another address (a call names one; 422 channel_not_allowed for
none). Its family is the call or text conversation the switches started from and every one linked from it. The
message goes in the family's conversation on that line that the agent holds, else in a new linked one the agent
holds, which takes a slot on the channel (409 agent_at_capacity; 409 conversation_open while another is open on
the line; a new WhatsApp one needs a template, 422 template_required). The family writes on a channel from one
sender (422 sender_mismatch), and a switch's sender is registered with PUT /numbers (422 from_not_allowed). In
wrap-up only files to the customer's own address go, and they stay here; any other switch is 409 in_wrap_up.
Plivo's refusal is 422 message_refused. A retry sends once only when it reuses its Idempotency-Key.

A second agent, available with a free slot (else 409): offered, and once it accepts it holds a slot and may
reply while the primary stays.

delete.description: The second agent leaves, to wrap-up if it is on; an open offer is withdrawn.

post.description:
The agent, or each team member, that is available with a free slot gets an offer (an agent that is not is
409); an agent or team transfer reads `transferring` until it ends. A cold transfer's first accept becomes the
primary and the current one goes to wrap-up, and keeps it if none accepts. A warm one's target joins as a second
agent until the transfer completes. A queue takes it now. An agent or team transfer needs a mode transfer.modes allows, else
409 transfer_mode_not_allowed.

Withdraw a transfer's open offers and end its warm target, which is told it was removed; 409 once the target has
taken the conversation. Its joined warm target may cancel it too, and leaves.
The warm target that joined becomes the primary and the current agent goes to wrap-up; 409 before it joined.

The agent read the conversation: unread_count reads 0 for every viewer until a message, note or voicemail no
agent wrote arrives, as after an agent reads its messages or writes in it.

One agent's disposition: an agent token's own, or the named agent's for a tenant key. It closes every
wrap-up the agent has on the conversation, and is 422 while the agent's newest stint there is live. The
conversation closes after its last wrap-up once the customer is gone.

Push the agent's own auto wrap-up deadline back, up to max_extend_sec in all; the stream carries the new
deadline.
`system: true` makes a locked row that the status map can point at.
The listed dispositions take the places they already hold, in the order given; the rest stay put.

delete.description:
Also deletes its sub-dispositions. Each stays as a deleted row, so the conversations filed under it keep their
disposition in reports, search and exports.

patch.description: `disabled` sets its sub-dispositions too, and a sub-disposition is disabled while its parent is.

get.description: Live events; resume with Last-Event-ID or ?after= (the header wins).

The agent, its desk settings, and its open text and task offers, so a desk that reloads can still answer
them (a call offer rings the phone instead). While Redis does not answer, the desk lists no offers.

post.description:
Presence: the second beat of a session applies the sign-in status; 40 s without one sets Offline. An HS
agent token is checked by the beat itself; a plugin's credential is resolved first.

The desk saw no activity for the settings' idle minutes: an available agent takes the idle status, which
takes no offers. One on any other status, or with a conversation offered or active on any channel, keeps it.

put.description:
The agent's new password, proved by its current one, whose failed tries count as a sign-in's. Every session of
the agent ends, this one too: the desk signs in again with the new password. A reset or a revoke that lands while
the change runs wins, and the change is 401.

delete.description: The agent signs out: as DELETE /agents/{id}/sessions.

post.description:
The next session of the agent's chain, so a desk renews before its tokens expire and never needs a new link.
The old tokens stay valid to their own expiry. 12 hours after the chain's first session, sign-in or mint, the
route is 403 sign_in_required; revoking the agent's sessions ends the chain at once.

A customer message from the tenant's gateway, on the open conversation for its (channel, from, to) or on its
email thread. It never opens one (404 no_open_conversation). A repeated provider_id answers 200 with the message
stored first, and tells of nothing.

get.description: A Plivo-hosted file of a customer message, for whoever holds its signed URL (an `` sends no header), fetched from Plivo with the tenant's credentials. `n` is read only once the signature vouches for it.

post.description: A delivery status from the tenant's gateway for an agent message; one that is not forward changes nothing.

put.description:
Checks at Plivo that the number is the Plivo account's, points it at the tenant's application unless `repoint` is
false or the tenant has none, stores it. An email address, a sender of the tenant's agent emails, is stored as it
is.

post.description: Take a text or task offer; a transfer's target becomes the conversation's primary. 422 once it is not open.

Turn down a text or task offer; the conversation's next round runs. An offer already over is 204 while a
transfer still offers the conversation, or while its queue stint has made a round, the next one running once no
offer is out; otherwise 422.

Hand a live call or a text contact to the queue. A Plivo form request (the queue's enqueue_url, query `agents`,
`context`, `consent_played=1`) gets XML; a tenant key's JSON gets the conversation's id. JSON with a text
`channel` is that channel's to read.

delete.description:
The recording goes at Plivo too, and with the call's last recording its legs' tracks. Plivo's verdict is the
answer, a refusal the job pool met included; a retry erases again whatever of the call is deleted here.

get.description:
The audio with HTTP Range, for whoever holds a signed URL that has not expired (an `<audio src>` sends no
header), fetched from Plivo with the tenant's credentials.

Each part's segments in time order, on the room recording's clock: the customer's, or the agent whose leg it
is. A track's start is its own, so its segments move by how long after the room's recording it began, and what a
track says before the room's recording or after its length is left out.
Each agent's seconds in each status, and in available and in away statuses, inside the window.
Each status change in the window, newest first, with how long the status lasted inside it.
Per bucket of the window in `tz`, the agents who changed to an available status in it.

The numbers of the conversations opened in the window, per `bucket` of their open time in `tz` (a week starts
on Sunday) and per value of each `by` key. A supervisor reads the whole tenant's numbers.

Each conversation opened in the window, newest first, with its numbers: the conversations the caller's role
sees, as its conversation list does.
The three fixed roles; a role's id is its name.

post.description:
An agent's session for its email and password in one tenant, as POST /agents/{id}/sessions mints it. Only an
install of one tenant may leave out `tenant_id`; elsewhere that is 409 tenant_required, before anything is checked.
A wrong email or password is one 401, as slow as the other; 10 failed tries of an email in a tenant, or 100 from
one client (an IPv6 one by its /64), in 15 minutes are 429 until the window ends.

patch.description: A JSON merge patch (RFC 7396) over the settings body; the whole result is validated before anything is saved.

get.description:
Newest first; a filter given several times takes any of its values. An agent lists the tasks assigned to it,
aimed at it or made by it; a supervisor also its teammates' and its teams'.

post.description:
Starts `todo`. An agent target takes it at once, routing `accepted`, or its routing reads `failed` when the
agent has no free slot and did not make it. A team task routes once the task is made, so its routing reads
`pending` here whatever its routing then finds.

get.description: The task with its activity in the order it was written: each note on its conversation and each change.

patch.description:
A change of status, priority, due date, schedule or target is activity and `task.updated`. Resolving or
cancelling ends the task's conversation. A new target or schedule, or `reroute`, takes it from its agent and
routes it again, a change of its routing status. 409 task_closed once it ended, and task_routing for a new target
or type or a reroute while an offer or a queue holds it, since a reassignment waits until its routing ends. 409
agent_at_capacity when the agent it goes to now has no free slot: it stays where it was.

post.description:
Registers a Plivo account, or a sub-account, by its Auth ID and Auth Token. Checks the credentials with Plivo,
points a new Plivo application at HS unless `plivo_app` is false, and seeds the tenant.

delete.description:
Refuse every credential of the tenant and cancel its pending Plivo commands, then remove the endpoints and
application HS made at Plivo.

patch.description:
Rename, replace the Plivo token (checked with Plivo first) and re-apply the app URLs from PUBLIC_BASE_URL to a
tenant's application.

get.description:
Every other agent with its status, `available` when that status is and it has a free slot on the channel,
`busy` when its slots there are full; and every team with its count of available agents. The unavailable and
the empty come last, then by name. A call also lists the tenant's saved destinations.

The views the caller sees, by type: new ones first, then the caller's order of that type. `favorite` lists the
caller's favorites in theirs.

put.description: Replaces the caller's order of one type of view, or its favorites, with these views.

patch.description: Merges the fields sent; a `filter` replaces the stored one.

get.description:
Closed conversations matching the view's stored filter, as `/conversations/search` returns them with its
columns as `fields`, so an agent or team deleted since still matches.

put.description: Puts the view first among the caller's favorites; 400 if it already is one.

post.description: The old secret stays valid for 24 h; meanwhile deliveries carry both signatures.

get.description:
The templates of the WhatsApp accounts in the settings, by name and language; `sender` keeps its account's
(404 sender_not_found), `status` those in it.

post.description: A menu's entry (its menu_url, where a tenant's app sends a call) or one attempt's input: a digit, or none.
Plivo's fetch for a `redirect` command: the caller left its room for room `r` and action `a`.

The caller left room `r` on Plivo's side. Plivo retries an exit whose answer it never got, and the exit has
moved the caller on by then, so the first answer is kept per call and room and a retry gets it again.

A voicemail's recording ended: keep it on the conversation, once per recording, and hang up. A mailbox id
counts only if it names the tenant's own queue or agent, and an agent's voicemail is told to that agent.

A call to one of the tenant's numbers: consent, then its entry point's open action, or in closed hours its
closed one. A number with no entry point is hung up. Plivo's retry for a call seated meanwhile gets the same
room, whatever the number or its hours say by then.

A ringing leg's progress binds it to its offer; its end before a join declines or misses the offer by Plivo's
cause code, kept on the offer. A joined leg's end is its leave, whether or not the room's exit event comes.

The caller's leg ended: call.ended, once per room, in whatever state the conversation is, then the caller is
gone unless someone said so first. V2 may call gone on the customer's MPC exit; call.ended belongs to /hangup.
A call no queue holds closes 10 s later, after any voicemail it left.

A customer's SMS or WhatsApp. It joins the open conversation for (channel, from, to); otherwise a number whose
open action is a queue opens one there, whatever its hours. Any other is dropped.
Plivo's delivery report for one outbound message; its MessageUUID fills one the send's reply never gave.
An event of room `r`: the caller's (seated, keyed, prompted, gone) or a member's (joined, left).

A room's recording or one leg's track is ready: kept once per Plivo recording, whatever the conversation's
state or room, unless empty or a mixed track, which is kept apart and told of to no one. A track that comes once
its call's recordings are all deleted goes at Plivo too.

A recording's transcript, kept on it; a replay of one kept already changes nothing. Timed segments for a
recording not kept yet wait for it. A voicemail's plain text is its transcript. Any other recording's plain
text, or none, is read from Plivo's timed segments later, the text kept for when Plivo has none.

get.description: Liveness for load balancers: only booleans, never exception text or hosts.
